title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
problem: When an LLM input contains multiple retrieved text chunks (as in RAG), the prefill phase that computes the KV cache dominates time-to-first-token (TTFT) and scales super-linearly with input length. Reusing precomputed KV caches for non-prefix chunks is broken because the precomputed KV ignores cross-attention with preceding chunks, which degrades generation quality. The paper asks how to quickly combine multiple independently precomputed KV caches so the result matches the quality of a full prefill recompute.
prior_limitations: Prefix caching (vLLM, SGLang, RAGCache) only reuses the KV cache of the first text chunk; when the LLM input contains many context chunks, savings are marginal and TTFT remains close to full KV recompute.

Full KV reuse (PromptCache) concatenates independently precomputed KV caches but ignores cross-attention between chunks, which causes large quality drops (F1 / Rouge-L) on multi-chunk RAG and multi-hop QA inputs.
Full KV reuse must precompute each chunk multiple times with dummy prefixes to preserve positional embedding, multiplying storage and precompute cost.
Most existing KV reuse work stores caches only in fast volatile memory (GPU HBM, CPU DRAM), limiting total cache capacity; emerging SSD-based reuse does not pipeline loading with compute.
Full KV recompute (standard prefill) is slow: ~3 s on Llama-34B and ~6 s on Llama-70B for a 4K-token input on a single A40 GPU.
contributions: Identifies that selective recomputation of a small subset of tokens' KV per layer is sufficient to recover cross-attention and match full-prefill quality, motivated by attention sparsity.
Defines KV deviation and attention deviation, and shows that recomputing the top-r% High-KV-Deviation (HKVD) tokens per layer minimizes attention deviation versus full recompute.
Proposes a gradual-filtering scheme that selects HKVD tokens layer by layer using the previous layer's KV deviation, avoiding the need to know the full-prefill KV cache.

Designs the CacheBlend system on top of vLLM that pipelines layer-wise selective KV recompute with KV-cache loading, so partial recompute incurs no extra TTFT delay and allows storing KV caches on slower devices (CPU RAM, SSD).
Introduces a loading controller that picks the recompute ratio and storage device by balancing recompute delay against KV load delay, with a quality lower-bound ratio (r* ~= 15%).

Empirically demonstrates 2.2-3.3x TTFT reduction and 2.8-5x throughput improvement over full KV recompute, with no more than 0.01-0.03 quality drop, across three models (Mistral-7B, Yi-34B, Llama-70B) and four datasets (2WikiMQA, Musique, SAMSum, MultiNews).
Releases an open-source implementation as part of LMCache (https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache).
method_summary: CacheBlend performs prefill layer by layer, but on each layer it only recomputes the K and V of a small subset of selected tokens (the High-KV-Deviation, or HKVD, tokens), reusing precomputed KV for the remaining tokens. HKVD tokens are identified via a gradual-filtering scheme: on each layer the system measures per-token KV deviation between the precomputed KV and the newly computed KV for the previously selected candidate set, keeps the top r_i% with highest deviation, and propagates that set to the next layer where r_{i+1} <= r_i, converging to the target average recompute ratio r (typically ~15%). The implementation, built on vLLM with ~3K lines of Python on PyTorch 2.0, exposes fetch_kv, prefill_layer, and synchronize interfaces, and uses two threads so that selective recompute of layer i is pipelined with KV loading of layer i+1 from CPU RAM or NVMe SSD. A loading controller picks the recompute ratio r and the storage device by estimating T_recompute(r%, LLM, L) = r% * Prefill(LLM, L) and T_load(LLM, L, device) = PerTokenKVSize(LLM) * L / Throughput(device), choosing the cheapest device whose load delay covers the recompute delay while keeping r at least the quality floor r* (15%). The KV-cache store hashes each input chunk (as vLLM does), evicts LRU when storage is full, and writes newly computed caches back to disk asynchronously.

datasets.name: 2WikiMQA
datasets.size: 200 test cases; contexts split into 512-token chunks with Langchain; prompt appended with 'Answer within 5 words.'

datasets.name: Musique
datasets.size: 150 test cases; contexts split into 512-token chunks with Langchain; prompt appended with 'Answer within 5 words.'
datasets.source: Trivedi et al., 2022 (Musique: Multihop questions via single-hop question composition)

datasets.name: SAMSum
datasets.size: 200 test cases; original 200-400 token chunks used

datasets.name: Musique Extended (synthetic)
datasets.size: 1500 original Musique queries + 4500 GPT-4-generated similar queries = 6000 queries; top-6 chunks of 512 tokens retrieved by L2 distance over SentenceTransformers embeddings; first 1K results skipped (cold cache)
datasets.source: Constructed by the authors from Musique using GPT-4 API and Langchain

datasets.name: 2WikiMQA Extended (synthetic)
datasets.size: 1500 original 2WikiMQA queries + 4500 GPT-4-generated similar queries = 6000 queries; top-6 chunks of 512 tokens retrieved by L2 distance over SentenceTransformers embeddings; first 1K results skipped (cold cache)
datasets.source: Constructed by the authors from 2WikiMQA using GPT-4 API and Langchain

hyperparameters.top_k_chunks_retrieved: 6 (top-6 by L2 distance over SentenceTransformers embeddings)
hyperparameters.quantization: 8-bit model quantization applied to Llama-70B and Yi-34B; Mistral-7B not quantized
hyperparameters.framework_version: vLLM with PyTorch v2.0; ~3K lines of Python
hyperparameters.kv_storage_levels: single level among CPU RAM or NVMe SSD (CPU DRAM hash table; LRU eviction)
hyperparameters.synthetic_query_generator: GPT-4 API (3 similar queries generated per seed query)
hyperparameters.batch_size: not stated (varied for sensitivity in Figure 15c; specific values not given)
hyperparameters.optimizer: not stated (no model training performed; inference-only system)

metrics.name: F1-score
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 7.1 Quality metrics: word-overlap F1 between model output and ground-truth answer, used for 2WikiMQA and Musique.

metrics.name: Rouge-L
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 7.1 Quality metrics: longest-common-subsequence based similarity, used for SAMSum and MultiNews (Lin, 2004, ROUGE package).

metrics.name: Time-to-first-token (TTFT)
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 2 / Section 7: prefill delay before the first generated token; primary latency metric.

metrics.name: Throughput
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 7.2 (Figure 14): requests served per unit time under varying request rates.

metrics.name: KV deviation Delta_kv(KV_i, KV_full_i)[j]
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 4.1: |KV_i[j] - KV_full_i[j]|; used internally to rank HKVD tokens.

metrics.name: Attention deviation Delta_attn(A_i, A_full_i)
metrics.definition_or_section: Section 4.1: L2 norm of the difference between forward attention matrices; minimization objective.

baselines.name: Full KV recompute (standard full prefill)
baselines.reported_score: TTFT reference: ~3 s for 4K tokens on Llama-34B and ~6 s on Llama-70B on one A40; CacheBlend reduces TTFT by 2.2-3.3x vs this baseline

baselines.name: Prefix caching (SGLang-style, idealized zero load delay)
baselines.reported_score: CacheBlend reduces TTFT by 2.2-3.3x and achieves 2.8-5x higher throughput vs this baseline; quality within 0.01-0.03 of this baseline

baselines.name: Full KV reuse (PromptCache-style)
baselines.reported_score: CacheBlend has ~same TTFT but 0.1-0.2 higher absolute F1 on QA and 0.03-0.25 higher absolute Rouge-L on summarization (Section 1); quality gap up to 0.15-0.35 in F1/Rouge-L (Section 7)

baselines.name: MapReduce (LangChain)
baselines.reported_score: CacheBlend has 2-5x lower TTFT and higher F1 than MapReduce (Figure 13)

baselines.name: MapRerank (LangChain)
baselines.reported_score: MapRerank has slightly lower TTFT than CacheBlend but much worse quality (Figure 13; exact numbers not stated in text)

compute_requirements: End-to-end experiments run on Runpod instances with 128 GB RAM, 2x NVIDIA A40 GPUs, and a 1 TB NVMe SSD measured at 4.8 GB/s throughput. Mistral-7B and Yi-34B are served on 1 A40 GPU; Llama-70B is served on 2 A40 GPUs. Llama-70B and Yi-34B use 8-bit quantization. Total training/wall-clock cost in GPU-hours is not stated; no training is performed (inference-only system).
open_questions: Exact batch sizes used in the main throughput experiments (Figure 14) are not stated; only sensitivity to batch size is discussed qualitatively (Figure 15c).
The exact quantization method (e.g., GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes) used for the 8-bit Llama-70B and Yi-34B is not specified.
The specific SentenceTransformers checkpoint used for retrieval embeddings is not named.
The exact F1 implementation (e.g., SQuAD-style token-level F1 vs LongBench's F1) is not cited beyond an informal reference; the paper points to a public notebook but does not pin a version.
The Rouge-L implementation library / version is not specified beyond citing the original ROUGE paper.
Total GPU-hours and dollar cost of the experiments are not reported.
The exact decay schedule for the gradual-filtering ratios (r1 > r2 > ... > r) is not given; only the qualitative rule is described.
The number of layers used for the first-layer HKVD selection step, and at which layers check_flag is True vs False, is not fully specified.
How CacheBlend behaves on models with non-RoPE positional encodings or non-transformer architectures (Mamba, Griffin) is explicitly left as future work.
Hyperparameters for the GPT-4 query-generation step used to build the Extended datasets (prompt, temperature, model version) are not given.
The exact prompt templates fed to the LLM for each dataset (beyond the appended 'Answer within 5 words.' for QA) are not provided.
